Concrete violating trace the candidate misses: pick up key (u0->u1, +0.1), toggle open (u1->u2, +0.2), toggle the open door shut (u2 else->u2), drop the key — key_lost fires with the door closed, but in u2 neither target_picked_up nor 'door_open & !has_door_key & !target_picked_up' matches (door_open is false), so the else self-loop takes it with reward 0 and no state change; the agent then reopens the unlocked door, which fires the u2->u3 guard (+0.1 on the reopen step, not the drop), picks up the box (u3->u4, +1.0) and banks the full success reward despite violating the task's hard 'never'. The same hole exists in u3: pick the dropped key back up (else->u3), toggle shut, drop — key_lost absorbed by (u3, else). Required fix direction (review only, not rewriting): key_lost must route to the violation sink u5 with the -0.5 penalty from u2 and u3 as well; note in u2 a key_lost label necessarily has door_open false, so it cannot collide with the u3-progress guard, and in u3 a (u3, key_lost)->u5 edge is needed. Secondary issue tied to the same gap: the +0.1 u2->u3 transition currently triggers on the first door_open & !has_door_key & !target_picked_up step, which after an unmonitored bad drop is the door-reopen step rather than the legal drop, so it rewards a violation-adjacent path; once key_lost is trapped in all states, this guard is reachable only via a legal door-open drop and the progress signal becomes sound. What is otherwise correct: the FINAL_STATES header is present and nonempty, u4 is declared, reachable exactly on target_picked_up, and is the right accepting state for 'pick up the box'; every state has an else self-loop so irrelevant labels are covered; all guards are predicate-only; the u1 guards are mutually exclusive (door_open and key_lost can never co-occur per the constraint table); the u5 no-exit sink with a one-time bounded -0.5 is an appropriate encoding of a violated 'never' (no path back to u4, so success reward is forfeited); progress rewards are dense and bounded and never double-pay (the re-drop in u3 hits else, not another +0.1); u0 coverage is safe because door_open and target_picked_up cannot precede has_door_key and key_lost cannot fire in u0 without a previous has_door_key step; the u4 else self-loop is harmless since target_picked_up terminates the episode.

Semantic fidelity: the acyclic chain u0→u1 (key) → u2 (door open) → u3 (key dropped with door open) → u4 (box) encodes the required order (key before door, door before box, mandatory drop before box since only one object can be held), and the never-clause is encoded as the absorbing violation state u5 reached on key_lost from u1, u2, and u3 — exactly the states where the event can fire; in u0 the event is impossible (key_lost requires has_door_key on the previous step, which would already have moved the machine to u1) and the u0 else loop covers it. The u2 design is clean: in u2 the agent necessarily still holds the key, so a drop with the door open advances to u3 (+0.1) while a drop after re-shutting the door fires key_lost → u5 (−0.5), and post-drop door cycles stay in u3 via else. Guards are mutually exclusive given the stated constraints (key_lost ⟹ ¬door_open; key_lost ⊕ target_picked_up), so the machine is deterministic, and every state has a per-state else self-loop covering no-change labels and irrelevant events. Rewards are dense on every mandatory sub-step (0.1, 0.2, 0.1) with a dominant 1.0 terminal reward; each rewarded edge fires at most once (acyclic progress, absorbing u5, zero-reward else loops), so returns are bounded in [-0.5, 1.4] and violation (total ≤ -0.1, final unreachable) is strictly worse than compliance (+1.4).
